text:
To my friends in Santander who celebrated
my professional appointment.


I ought now to say, “Friends,
thank you,” and sit down, without filler rhymes.
Allow me to say it in a lyrical tone,
in verse, yes, but free and fanciful.
Friends:
in a few days I will find myself surrounded by boys,
clumsy boys and clever ones,
gentle and prickly,
many leagues from my Santander,
in an ancient town,
quiet
and cold,
and I will speak to them of verse and half-lines,
and Dante, and Shakespeare, and Moratín the son,
and pluperfects and participles,
and one will yawn and another wink at me.
And another, surely the cleverest,
will give me a final nickname.
And so monotonous, lengthy school years will pass.
But one day I will have a pupil,
a true pupil,
and shape his child’s soul
and make him become new and different,
different from me and everyone: himself.
And he will keep respect and affection for me.
And now I say to you:
Friends,
let us drink to that boy,
to that chosen pupil,
that my stiff fingers
may shape his spirit well,
and my lyrical flame catch in his virgin heart,
and that he may follow his way
whole and clear,
and because this pupil of mine,
who will immortalize my name and surname,
…may be the son,
the son
of one of you, my friends.
